newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi plans new push for social order and security.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi plans new push for social order and security.

text.p: Vietnam is planning to intensify its drive to ensure social order and the defeat of hostile forces intent on political and ideological sabotage, state-controlled media reports said on Tuesday.
The Hanoi police journal Capital Security said the Ministry of Interior had issued a seven-point plan for civil control during the lunar new year festivities in February.

The plan included a blitz on hooligans, hitmen, prostitutes, drug addicts and gamblers and renewed efforts to stamp out corruption and smuggling. It also called for tighter control of video tape rental services and restaurants and guest houses suspected of doubling as vice dens.
The Communist Party daily Nhan Dan said the Hanoi party committee had agreed to step up "political security" in the capital, including control over foreigners.
"It should work out many appropriate ways to educate party members, cadres and people about hostile forces' plots and ploys aimed at political and ideological sabotage," the paper said.
The term "hostile forces", in party parlance, usually refers to forces intent on subverting the country's political regime.
